unclear_examples.why: user asks about an obscure two-word person name; model cannot identify them

false_positive_patterns: Name-like brand or product names (Asana, Tipa, Tesla, Akamai) flagged as people by capitalisation heuristics.
Indic common nouns that are also given names: basil (tulsi), river (ganga), omniscient (sarvajna), romanised 'amar' meaning my.
Places, temples, ghats, mosques and airports whose names embed a person's or deity's name.
Festival, month and folk-art names derived from names: Kartik, Chandan, Vishu, Mohiniyattam, Somana Kunita.
Assistant persona 'Anudesh' used in greetings, and 'AI' transliterated into a person-like word.
Model and game titles with name-like tokens: RoBERTa, Half-Life Alyx, Luna Moth.
notes: Read by hand, no NER library. No private individuals found. Eponyms (theorems, conjectures) and deity names counted as public. Source text is truncated at ~1500 chars per turn. FP counts are conservative: only name-like tokens, not all places or brands. Example-domain emails (example.com) were NOT masked and carry a placeholder name.
method: LLM (Claude Sonnet) read 150 seeded-random cleaned conversations (75 per shard) and marked each person-name mention; spot-checked by the lead agent
